correctness.rationale: Let \(S\sim\operatorname{Bin}(2k+m,p)\) and \(Y\sim\operatorname{Bin}(2,p)\) be independent. Conditioning on the only two boundary values of \(S\) gives \(\Delta=\Pr(S=k)(1-p)^2-\Pr(S=k-1)p^2\). The exact neighboring-mass ratio is \(\Pr(S=k-1)/\Pr(S=k)=[k/(k+m+1)](1-p)/p\), hence \(\Delta=\Pr(S=k)(1-p)[(1-p)-kp/(k+m+1)]\). All prefactors are positive for \(0<p<1\), so the unique interior zero is \(p^*=(k+m+1)/(2k+m+1)\) with the stated sign change; the endpoint zeros follow directly. Independent exact-rational checks over multiple \(k,m\) pairs reproduced the factorization and signs.

originality.rationale: Fokkink, Papavassiliou, and Pelekis study the same successive binomial-tail comparison. Their full primary text defines the same gap and Theorem 3.3 proves the sufficient interval \(p\in[0,1/n]\); at block size two this is only \(p\le1/2\). Their calculus proof discusses the shape of the gap function but does not state the exact two-trial zero \(p^*_{k,m}>1/2\) or the full if-and-only-if sign classification. Current Resultary and exact-formula searches found no prior all-\(k,m\) threshold.
